name: Mohatta Palace Museum
funding: The Government of Sindh owns the palace, bought by the federal government after 1980. A board of trustees oversees it, and entry costs Rs 30.
watch: Opened in September 1999 with Treasures of the Talpurs. In 2021 the Sindh High Court ordered a medical college there; the government appealed.
records_note: Posts audited accounts for 2013 to 2018 and names all its trustees; no annual reports or donor list are published.

name: Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy
funding: Statutory body under the Ministry of Cultural Affairs, founded in 1974, governed by a minister-led Executive Council. It runs district branches, scholarships and the National Art Gallery.
watch: The venue for most Dhaka Art Summit editions, which the Samdani foundation produces.
records_note: Its government portal lists the director general, officers, projects, laws and notices; no annual reports, accounts, funder list or governing council are posted.

name: Pejman Foundation (Argo Factory)
funding: Private non-profit founded in 2015 by collector and film producer Hamidreza Pejman, who bought the Argo Factory brewery in 2016.
watch: Argo Factory is closed until further notice; the war began on 28 February 2026. Pejman says an unnamed body shut its film series over permits.
records_note: Argo Factory names three in-kind sponsors on an undated page, and lists staff but no board; no reports or accounts are published.

name: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art (TMoCA)
funding: State museum owned by the arts deputy of Iran's Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance, which OFAC lists as an entity. The state set a 16.5 billion toman renovation budget.
watch: After 1979 the state kept its Western collection in storage. In 2017 the culture minister cancelled its Berlin and Rome loan show.
why_flagged: State museum owned by the arts deputy of Iran's Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance, which OFAC lists as an entity. The state set a 16.5 billion toman renovation budget.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board; its site only names the Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance as the owner.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA)
funding: Government of India. A subordinate office of the Ministry of Culture, founded in 1954, with branches in Mumbai and Bengaluru.
watch: In 2000 the Culture Ministry ordered a painting pulled and all the artists withdrew. In 2019 members cut off Amol Palekar's criticism of the ministry.
why_flagged: Run as a subordinate office of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, since its 1954 opening, with centres in Mumbai and Bengaluru. No sponsor is listed.
records_note: It posts nothing itself; its parent Ministry of Culture publishes annual reports from 2014-15 to 2023-24, with no sponsor list or advisory board named.

name: Israel Museum
funding: American Friends of the Israel Museum raised over $450M since 1972. Mandel and Safra foundations each gave $12M in 2009. The 2025 report filed with the Israeli register puts state and city grants at 21 percent of income and donations at 27 percent, mostly from abroad, with 39 percent from sources the register does not describe.
watch: In July 2009 PACBI, the Palestinian BDS campaign, urged Yinka Shonibare in an open letter not to guest-curate here. He held a 2010 show.
why_flagged: American Friends of the Israel Museum raised over $450M since 1972. Mandel and Safra foundations each gave $12M in 2009. The 2025 report filed with the Israeli register puts state and city grants at 21 percent of income and donations at 27 percent, mostly from abroad, with 39 percent from sources the register does not describe.
records_note: Its website would not load; a search shows a named board page, and the Israeli register lists it as a public benefit company.

name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
funding: Paulson Family Foundation gave $15M in 2021 and the Eyal & Marilyn Ofer Family Foundation $5M in 2019.
watch: In September 2025 over 50 artists signed an open letter asking two exhibiting artists to cancel their show, citing Gaza. The director rejected cancelling exhibitions.
why_flagged: Paulson Family Foundation gave $15M in 2021 and the Eyal & Marilyn Ofer Family Foundation $5M in 2019. No sponsor list found on its site.
records_note: Its annual report link returns an error; it posts no accounts or donor list, and its trustees page names the board, undated.

name: Haifa Museum of Art
funding: Municipal museum group Haifa Museums. Site logos: Haifa Municipality, Ministry of Culture and Sport, Mizrahi Tefahot bank. Japan's embassy gave NIS 15,620 for a 2025 Tikotin show.
watch: In January 2019 hundreds protested the loaned McJesus sculpture. Minister Regev threatened to defund the museum; a deputy attorney general rebuked her. It was removed.
why_flagged: Municipal museum group Haifa Museums. Site logos: Haifa Municipality, Ministry of Culture and Sport, Mizrahi Tefahot bank. Japan's embassy gave NIS 15,620 for a 2025 Tikotin show.
records_note: No reports or accounts; the sponsorship page names one 2025 foreign-state donor, the Embassy of Japan, beside logos, and the board of directors is listed.

name: Petach Tikva Museum of Art
funding: Friends association (2015) funds shows and acquisitions via 1,800 NIS memberships and a 23,000 NIS patron tier. British Friends of the Art Museums of Israel back programmes. No budget published.
watch: In 2014 the municipality called on the museum to close Arkadi Zaides's Archive; the New York Review of Books reports the museum refused.
records_note: The Friends association board is listed with Reut Ferster as chair; the museum publishes no reports, accounts or donor names.

name: Arab-Hebrew Theatre of Jaffa (Al-Saraya)
funding: Partly funded by Israel's Ministry of Culture and the Tel Aviv Municipality. In 2017 co-director Igal Ezrati put public funds at nearly NIS 900,000, a significant share of its budget.
watch: Police barred two film screenings in 2024, the theatre told the High Court. In 2017 Minister Regev asked the Finance Ministry to cut funding.
why_flagged: Partly funded by Israel's Ministry of Culture and the Tel Aviv Municipality. In 2017 co-director Igal Ezrati put public funds at nearly NIS 900,000, a significant share of its budget.
records_note: Its site shows no reports or donors; the public board of 27 is listed, and filings sit in the Israeli nonprofit register.

name: Dar Jacir for Art and Research
funding: Kickstarter raised nearly $24,000 in 2017. A.M. Qattan Foundation, Sida-funded, announced a $255,691 grant via the Institute for Palestine Studies in March 2018. AFAC lists three grants.
watch: Its owners said Israeli soldiers raided it on 15 May 2021 and took equipment, per Hyperallergic. Emily Jacir and Aline Khoury co-direct it.
records_note: Posts yearly Donors and Partners pages naming supporters, with named text through 2020; no annual reports, accounts or board are published.

name: Diriyah Biennale Foundation
funding: Created in 2020 by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Culture; the culture minister chairs its board.
watch: Runs the Diriyah Contemporary Art Biennale and the Islamic Arts Biennale in Jeddah. The foundation says the first Islamic Arts Biennale drew over 600,000 visitors.
why_flagged: Created in 2020 by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Culture; the culture minister chairs its board. No budget or sponsor list found.
records_note: Its website returned a block page, so reports, accounts, partners and board could not be checked.
